items.label: section_header
items.text: THERMODYNAMICANDKINETICSTABILITY

items.label: text
items.text: The reactionbetween methane and oxygen is exothermic,and the total entropy change has a positivevalue:

items.label: formula
items.text:
CH₄(g) + 2O₂(g) → CO₂(g) + 2H₂O(l)   ΔH꜀° = −890.3 kJ mol⁻¹
ΔS_total = +2.95 kJ mol⁻¹

items.label: text
items.text: Since △Stotal is positive,the reaction is thermodynamically feasible at 298K. However, the reaction doesnottakeplaceuntil thereactionmixtureisignited,usuallywithaflame.

items.label: text
items.text: The added heat energy is required to overcome the high activation energy of the reaction.

items.label: text
items.text: A reaction mixture with a high activation energy, where a reaction will not take place spontaneously atroomtemperature,issaidtobekineticallystable

items.label: text
items.text: You can see here that a reaction mixture (such as methane and oxygen) canbe thermodynamically unstablebut kinetically stable,so a reaction doesnot take place under standard conditions.

items.label: section_header
items.text: THEROLEOFTEMPERATURE

items.label: text
items.text: The increase in entropy obtained by supplying a certain amount of heat energy to an object depends on thetemperatureofthesystem.

items.label: text
items.text: If an object is very cold, the molecules are not moving around very much.Supplying some heat energy tothe objectwill make themoleculesmove around more,so theentropy increases.

items.label: text
items.text: If we supply the same amount of heat energy to a much hotter object, the entropy will still increase, but not by as much as with the cold object. This is because in the hot object the molecules are already moving around vigorously and the increased degree of movement is less for the hot object.

items.label: section_header
items.text: WHYDOESWATERFREEZE?

items.label: text
items.text: We will now apply these principles to explain why,under certain conditions, water will freeze.

items.label: text
items.text: Ice has lower entropy than liquid water, so Ssystem is negative.

items.label: text
items.text: The process is exothermic, so △Ssuroundings is positive.

items.label: text
items.text: If the magnitude of Ssuroundings > the magnitude of Ssystem, then Siotal is positive and the water will freeze.
